note: Written by scripts/sim/calibrate.mjs. Do not edit by hand.

ub1g.note: Buoyant flow at 1 g in cm/s. NTRS 20170006615 gives about 20 cm/s (anchor A1) and 17 cm/s for the smallest rod (A2). Rods only.

mixExponent.note: Exponent n in U_eff = (U_f^n + U_b^n)^(1/n). 4 from the derivation in NTRS 20200000557 (S1), 1 from the linear sum in NTRS 20170006615 (S2). Sampled between them.

o2Int.note: Oxygen where the blow-off line reaches zero flow, percent. 13.3 (A5), 13.4 (A6), lowest BASS-II test point 13.6. PMMA rods.

o2Blowoff1g.note: Oxygen at the 1 g blow-off limit, percent (A3, quarter-inch PMMA rod). Fixes the slope of the blow-off line, so the 1 g limit for rods is 16% by construction.

sb.note: Sharpness of the blow-off edge, per unit of ln(flow).

uFloor.note: Smallest effective flow in cm/s, so ln(U) stays finite when forced flow and gravity are both zero.

uZeroReading.note: cm/s assigned to BASS-II extinctions where the air display read 0 or <1. Used only when building the data points.

gamma.note: Rise of ln(U_q) per percentage point of O2 below the reference. Fitted to BASS-II points.

sq.note: Sharpness of the low-flow edge, per unit of ln(flow). Fitted to BASS-II points.

lnUq0.note: ln of the quench flow in cm/s at the reference O2, per material. Fitted to BASS-II points.

dirShift.note: Shift of ln(U_q) for concurrent versus opposed flow. Fitted with a penalty toward zero.

beta.note: Change in ln(U_q) per unit of ln(thickness in mm), shared by PMMA film and slab. Thicker samples quench at higher flow when positive.

defaultThickness.note: mm, used when no thickness is given. Close to the middle of the thicknesses in the data.

gravSigmaMax.note: Extra log-normal spread on U_b at high gravity. No outcome data exists at any gravity above zero, so the band widens with g.

gravSigmaScale.note: Gravity in g at which the extra spread reaches 63% of its maximum.

burnThreshold.note: Mean P(burn) at or above this is labelled "burns".

extinguishThreshold.note: Mean P(burn) at or below this is labelled "extinguishes". In between is "marginal".

anchors.source: Mixed convection blowoff limits as a function of oxygen concentration and upward forced stretch rate for burning PMMA rods of various sizes (Marcum, Ferkul, Olson, ICES-2017-370)
anchors.quote: in good agreement with normal gravity buoyant flow velocities (~ 20 cm/s)
anchors.howUsed: Centre of the 1 g buoyant flow range (15 to 25 cm/s).
anchors.caveat: Second-hand: the paper cites an older measurement. Not a rod-specific value.

anchors.source: Mixed convection blowoff limits as a function of oxygen concentration and upward forced stretch rate for burning PMMA rods of various sizes (Marcum, Ferkul, Olson, ICES-2017-370)
anchors.quote: an effective forced flow of 17 cm/s
anchors.quantity: Buoyant stretch expressed as forced flow, smallest rod (radius 0.318 cm)
anchors.howUsed: Lower end of the 1 g buoyant flow range.
anchors.caveat: Found by shifting the 1 g blow-off data onto the BASS-II boundary, so it is not independent of the 16% figure in A3.

anchors.source: Combustion of Solids in Microgravity: Results from the BASS-II Experiment (poster, Ferkul et al., 2014)
anchors.quote: The 1g blowoff for the ¼" rod is at 16% oxygen
anchors.quantity: Oxygen at the 1 g blow-off limit
anchors.howUsed: Fixes where the blow-off line crosses the 1 g buoyant flow, so the 1 g limit for rods is 16% by construction.
anchors.caveat: Applied to all four materials, which is an assumption. Precision of the 16% is not stated.

anchors.source: Mixed convection blowoff limits as a function of oxygen concentration and upward forced stretch rate for burning PMMA rods of various sizes (Marcum, Ferkul, Olson, ICES-2017-370)
anchors.quote: the normal gravity blowoff boundary for this axisymmetric rod geometry is determined to be linear, with oxygen concentration directly proportional to flow speed
anchors.howUsed: Blow-off side is a straight line in oxygen against flow.
anchors.caveat: Rods only. The paper discards its 14% data as anomalous.

anchors.source: Microgravity flammability of PMMA rods in concurrent flow (Olson and Ferkul, 9th US National Combustion Meeting, 2015)
anchors.quote: Using the y-intercept of the linear fit (13.3 % O2 in the Figure 4 fit, versus the minimum test point of 13.6 % O2)
anchors.quantity: Zero-stretch intercept of the BASS-II blow-off line
anchors.howUsed: Intercept of the blow-off line, sampled between 13.3 and 13.6%.

anchors.source: Mixed convection blowoff limits as a function of oxygen concentration and upward forced stretch rate for burning PMMA rods of various sizes (Marcum, Ferkul, Olson, ICES-2017-370)
anchors.quote: estimates that 13.4% O2 is the limiting oxygen concentration below which the fuel cannot burn at any stretch rate
anchors.quantity: Zero-stretch limit from the 1 g blow-off line
anchors.caveat: Rods only. Described by the authors as a conservative estimate.

anchors.source: Buoyancy Effects on Concurrent Flame Spread Over Thick PMMA
anchors.quote: the mixed convective flow velocity can be obtained by equating the boundary layer thickness for the mixed convective flow
anchors.quantity: Rule for combining forced flow and buoyant flow (Eq. 6: U_m = U_f (P/P0) [g^2 l_p^2 / U_f^4 + 1]^(1/4))
anchors.howUsed: Central combination rule: U_eff = (U_f^4 + U_b^4)^(1/4). The sampled range runs from a linear sum to this rule.
anchors.caveat: The equation was read from the rendered page, not extracted as text. Derived for flame spread rate, not for flammability limits. The paper also scales by P/P0, which this model does not.

anchors.source: Mixed convection blowoff limits as a function of oxygen concentration and upward forced stretch rate for burning PMMA rods of various sizes (Marcum, Ferkul, Olson, ICES-2017-370)
anchors.quote: An empirical linear superposition of the buoyant stretch rate of ab=80 s-1 is used to align the data
anchors.quantity: Alternative rule for combining forced flow and buoyant flow
anchors.howUsed: Lower end of the sampled combination exponent (linear sum).
anchors.caveat: Empirical, rods only, and the flows are aligned (upward forced flow with upward buoyancy).

anchors.source: Microgravity flammability of PMMA rods in concurrent flow (Olson and Ferkul, 9th US National Combustion Meeting, 2015)
anchors.quote: the quenching branch is captured with a red dashed exponential fit
anchors.howUsed: Supports the exponential rise of the quench flow as oxygen falls, as in the model.

anchors.quote: In the normal gravity screening tests, flames extinguish by blowoff, where the buoyant flow is too fast
anchors.howUsed: Supports reading the 1 g limit as a blow-off limit.

anchors.source: Combustion of Solids in Microgravity: Results from the BASS-II Experiment (poster, Ferkul et al., 2014)
anchors.quote: we obtained steady spreading at 13.6% oxygen in BASS-II
anchors.quantity: Lowest oxygen with steady spreading in microgravity
anchors.howUsed: Model nose of the rod flammability boundary should sit near here.
anchors.caveat: Also appears in A5 and A6, which are used for the intercept. The quench side of the nose is not.

anchors.quote: reduced-g buoyancy or spacecraft ventilation flows of 5-20 cm/s
anchors.quantity: Flow level in reduced gravity (0 g, Lunar g, Martian g)
anchors.howUsed: Model buoyant flow at 0.165 g and 0.38 g should fall inside this range.
anchors.caveat: Mixes buoyancy with ventilation, so it is a plausibility range only.

anchors.source: Combustion of Solids in Microgravity: Results from the BASS-II Experiment (poster, Ferkul et al., 2014)
anchors.quote: the material has a negative Oxygen Margin of Safety of 2.4% O2
anchors.quantity: Gap between the 1 g limit and the microgravity minimum
anchors.howUsed: Model margin (1 g limit minus nose) compared with 1.4 to 2.4.
anchors.caveat: Equals 16% minus 13.6%, so it is partly the same data as A3 and H1.

anchors.quote: PMMA rods: Negative Oxygen Margin of Safety = 1.4% O2
anchors.quantity: Gap between the 1 g limit and the microgravity minimum
anchors.howUsed: Second, lower margin figure from a later briefing.
anchors.caveat: The two margins differ and the sources do not say why.

anchors.source: Combustion of Solids in Microgravity: Results from the BASS-II Experiment (poster, Ferkul et al., 2014)
anchors.quantity: Radiative quenching flow, 0.1 mm PMMA film
anchors.howUsed: Model film quench flow at 21% O2 should be under 2 cm/s.
anchors.caveat: Oxygen level is not stated for this sequence.

anchors.source: Combustion of Solids in Microgravity: Results from the BASS-II Experiment (poster, Ferkul et al., 2014)
anchors.howUsed: Model blow-off flow for the film should bracket 40 cm/s over the BASS-II oxygen range.
anchors.caveat: Oxygen level is not stated for this sequence. Loose check only.

anchors.source: Flammability Aspects of a Cotton-Fiberglass Fabric in Opposed and Concurrent Airflow in Microgravity (Ferkul, 2013)
anchors.quote: Downward flame spread (opposed flow) in 1-g with this material is not possible in normal air.
anchors.quantity: Outcome at 1 g, opposed flow, in air
anchors.howUsed: Model chance of burning for SIBAL, opposed, 1 g, 21% O2 should be below 50%.
anchors.caveat: A qualitative outcome. It is the only 1 g outcome found for opposed flow. The SAFFIRE-II ground tests (PSI-99) cover concurrent flow.
